title: Freya and the Sigil Again
premise: When the crown's witch-hunters sweep the Thornfell passes, runaway apprentice Oscar Oyelaran is forced to guide a ragged caravan of gifted fugitives along the smugglers' roads she swore she'd never use again. Among them travels a mute child bearing a living sigil burned into his skin—a seal that, if broken, would free the war-god buried beneath the mountains. Oscar discovers the hunters aren't hunting witches at all; they're herding the gifted toward the sigil to break it. In the final confrontation at the moon-thirteenth turning, Oscar must choose between destroying the sigil and herself with it or trusting her found family to carry the burden together—and she chooses trust, shattering the sigil across thirteen willing bearers so no single soul can ever be hunted for it again.
about_author: Hazel Halloran is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain trails before trading ink for fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by knowing the way out.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Three years after fleeing her hedge-witch mistress, Oscar lives as a mule-train guide, hiding small magics in knotwork and trail-markings. When a royal proclamation nails every tavern door—gifted persons to be registered—the old fear of being seen returns. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility made suddenly, brutally clear.

chapters.title: Smoke on the North Pass
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She finds her old village burned and her mistress Maren dying of hunter-wrought wounds. Maren presses a map fragment into her hands and names a sanctuary: the Hollow of Thirteenth Moon. Grief and guilt collide as Oscar realizes Maren hid things from her too. Emotional beat: inheritance of both love and danger.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hired by smuggler Brannic Ferro for one last run, Oscar discovers the 'cargo' is seven fugitives—including a mute boy, Tam, whose forearm bears a shifting black sigil that hums when hunters near. She wants to refuse; the coin is survival. Emotional beat: complicity begins before consent does.

chapters.title: What the Sigil Sings
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, first time. Inside his silence, the sigil speaks in images: a buried god, chains of oath-stone, thirteen moons. He trusts only Oscar, who doesn't flinch from him. Meanwhile the caravan argues about abandoning the boy. Emotional beat: loneliness answered by an unlikely ally.

chapters.title: The Toll-Keeper's Riddle
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At a mountain toll-bridge, a half-mad gatekeeper demands payment in truths, not coin. Oscar lies about her gift and the bridge nearly drops the caravan into the gorge; only Tam's sigil steadies the stones. The group now knows what he carries. Emotional beat: secrets have structural costs.

chapters.title: Brannic's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Flashback chapter: how Brannic came to owe the Hollow's founder a life-debt, and why he agreed to move Tam. His pragmatism masks terror—he lost a daughter to the first hunt. Emotional beat: hard men are made of grief, not stone.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Heather
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Crown witch-hunters led by Captain Ilse Varga ambush the caravan on open moor. Two fugitives die covering the escape. Oscar uses forbidden battle-craft Maren taught her and hates how easily it returns. Emotional beat: survival requires becoming something you promised not to be.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Reads Ash
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. The captain examines the ambush site and reads Oscar's signature in the burn patterns. She recognizes the technique—an academy style thought extinct. Her orders, we learn, come not from the crown but from a masked patron called the Custodian. Emotional beat: the hunter has her own leash.

chapters.title: Salt Caves and Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third among three fugitives: a healer named Wren, an old soldier Doss, and twin sisters fleeing together. Around a salt-cave fire they build rituals of belonging—shared meals, name-telling. Oscar watches from the edge, wanting in. Emotional beat: found family forms in the ordinary moments.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. An astronomer-fugitive confirms the moon completes its thirteenth turn in nineteen days—the night the sigil can be unbound. Tam's marks spread up his arm; he's in pain. Oscar decodes Maren's map fragment: the Hollow isn't a sanctuary, it's where the god is buried. Emotional beat: the destination was always the trap.

chapters.title: The Road Nobody Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She leads the caravan off all maps onto a smuggler's route her mistress made her memorize as a child, through a drowned mine. The passage floods; Doss nearly drowns saving the twins. Oscar admits she chose this road to avoid the Hollow, buying time. Emotional beat: leadership means confessing your fear.

chapters.title: Varga's Offer
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. The captain corners Oscar alone under a parley flag. She offers amnesty for the whole caravan if Oscar delivers Tam to the Custodian—revealing the Custodian believes breaking the sigil will restore a golden age. Varga genuinely believes it too. Emotional beat: the enemy makes a real argument.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar tells the caravan everything—the Hollow, the thirteenth turn, Varga's offer. The group fractures: some want to trade Tam; Wren defends him fiercely. Tam, hearing himself discussed like cargo, walks into the snow. Emotional beat: truth tested against loyalty, and loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Chose
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Found by Oscar in a shrine ruin, Tam breaks his silence using borrowed words scratched in frost: he chooses to go to the Hollow—not to be saved, but because the god inside the sigil shows him the hunters' true plan: not freedom, but a weapon reforged. Emotional beat: the protected becomes the deciding voice.

chapters.title: Reunion of Runaways
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The caravan reaches the Hollow and finds it populated—hundreds of hidden gifted, including, shockingly, Maren alive, healed by the Hollow's ambient magic but bound to its founder's will. Reunion curdles as Oscar learns Maren sent the hunters' proclamation rumor herself, to flush runaways toward safety. Emotional beat: rescue that feels like betrayal.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The Hollow's ancient founder explains the choice: on the thirteenth turn, the sigil must be either destroyed (killing its bearer) or transferred whole to a volunteer vessel who becomes the god's eternal prison. Maren volunteers. Oscar refuses to let her. Emotional beat: love arguing with sacrifice.

chapters.title: Night of Knives and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Varga's hunters assault the Hollow, guided by a traitor within—one of the twins, who traded information for her sister's registration papers. Battle in the lantern-lit caverns; Brannic falls holding the gate. Emotional beat: the family bleeds, and forgiveness begins mid-fight.

chapters.title: The Custodian Unmasked
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar confronts the Custodian atop the burial vault and unmasks them: the last surviving archivist of the old war, who broke the original seal deliberately, believing a caged god corrupts everything near it. Varga, seeing the Custodian's planned weapon-reforging, turns her hunters aside. Emotional beat: enemy and ally swap places in a single revelation.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Thirteen Hands
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax. On the thirteenth turn, Oscar proposes the impossible: split the sigil into thirteen fragments borne by thirteen volunteers—herself, Tam, Maren, Wren, Doss, Varga, and others—so no bearer is a target and no hand can wield the god alone. The rite begins as the vault collapses. Emotional beat: the thesis made flesh—survival shared is survival.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Snow
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Mid-rite, the god speaks through the splitting sigil, offering each bearer their deepest want. Each refuses in turn—thirteen small acts of defiance. Tam, closest to the god's voice, answers it with his own name, spoken aloud for the first time. The god sleeps, unchained but uninvited. Emotional beat: identity as the ultimate refusal.

chapters.title: After the Turning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Burials, reckonings, the traitor twin forgiven by her sister and exiled by her own choice. The crown's hunt collapses without the Custodian's gold. The thirteen bearers feel the sigil faintly warm whenever another is near—a compass of belonging. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing a grave.

chapters.title: Every Smuggler's Road Home
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing. Spring on the Thornfell passes. Oscar reopens the roads openly, guiding refugees instead of hiding them, Maren beside her and Tam chattering in full sentences. A new proclamation goes up on tavern doors—not a hunt, but an invitation. She signs her name beneath it. Emotional beat: visibility chosen at last, and it costs nothing but courage.
